sections.title: Interaction (Wave U)
sections.note: General Planner behaviour — WPs U1–U7. The recommended option is what gets built if you do not answer.

questions.q: Hidden things cannot be clicked. Should drawing tools also stop SNAPPING to hidden items?
questions.why: Selection, hover, right-click and box-select ignore hidden layers after U1. Snapping is different: you may hide a wall layer on purpose and still draw along it.

opts.d: Hidden = cannot be selected, hovered, menu'd or boxed. Wall and box snapping keep working on hidden geometry.
A hidden box is never snapped to or linked by the path tool. Walls still snap.
Hidden walls stop snapping too. Strict, but drawing on a hidden construction layer becomes impossible.

questions.q: Selection glow when SEVERAL pieces are selected?
questions.why: One selected piece gets the soft aura (U2). Multi-selection today shows a blue circle per piece.

opts.d: Aura for a single selection only; multi keeps today's circles.
Consistent look; busier screen with many pieces.

questions.q: How do you move the selection by keyboard once W A S D / Q / E are always the camera?
questions.why: IJKL collides with J (mark wall) and K (circuit pick); Ctrl+Shift+W closes the browser window.

opts.t: Shift + W A S D, Shift + Q / E
opts.d: 100 mm steps, 10 mm in fine mode (F held or the lock). No other key changes meaning.

opts.t: I J K L + U / O
opts.d: A second cluster for the right hand; J and K tools move to other letters (mark wall → M, circuit pick → C).
Shift+arrows move, plain arrows keep height / cycling. Shift+↑/↓ is today's 10 mm lift, so lift would need another key.

questions.q: Keep a setting that brings back the old 'WASD moves the selection' behaviour?

opts.d: Settings → 'Régi billentyűk'. Off by default; removed in a later round.
Cleaner; no way back if the new layout bothers you.

questions.q: What should the toolbar '⤢ Full view' button do after Tab exists?

opts.d: Tab = everything (sidebars + rail + inspector); the button keeps hiding only the two sidebars.
One meaning; the button becomes the mouse version of Tab.

questions.q: 'Falak egyesítve' — on or off by default once it works in translucent mode?

opts.d: Nothing changes until you tick it.
Existing projects keep their setting.

sections.title: Walls and openings (Wave G)
sections.note: G1 moves the golden renders (once, deliberately); G2 rewrites wall ends after a dry run.

questions.q: Wide doors and windows — which look?
questions.why: MATERIAL §7. Door: a white gap through the whole wall with jambs and the swing arc. Window: a pale-blue pane inset ≈ 12 % from each face, with a double glass line, no arc.

opts.d: Door = gap + swing; window = inset pane + double glass line.

opts.t: No swing arc in the Normal view
opts.d: Arcs only in the Blueprint; the working view stays calmer.
Doors and windows differ only by fill colour and the glass line.

questions.q: Wall refine — what is the exact form of a junction?
questions.why: Measured on P33 teszt v2: 27 junctions (12 L, 15 T), 33 moves, max 308 mm; 12 ends sit on the partner's centreline (the wall tool's snap), which leaves a notch at outer corners.

opts.t: L = full corner square, T = stem butts on the face
opts.d: Every corner is the square of the two walls; every T stem stops exactly on the through wall's face. One house style.
Per junction, the exact form that needs the least movement (ties → A). Respects how each corner was drawn; mixed styles remain.

opts.t: L = square, T = stem through to the far face
opts.d: T stems overlap the whole thickness of the through wall.

questions.q: Wall refine — scope and rounding

opts.t: Visible, unlocked walls; round to 1 mm first
opts.d: The plan's fractional coordinates (from turning it 180°) become whole millimetres; equal values stay equal.
Coordinates stay fractional; refine is exact but a second run may still find sub-mm moves.

opts.t: Every wall of the level, hidden ones too
opts.d: Hidden walls are refined as well.

sections.title: Stack (Wave S)
sections.note: Layer menus, RBX, BASE, route following, security.

questions.q: Security (Home Assistant / ESPHome): how are the detectors wired?
questions.why: Classic alarm practice is a star to one protected controller (a cut cable is detectable, tamper loops possible). The RBX already holds an ESPHome node, but it is reachable and serves comfort functions.

opts.t: Star to the SSC (ESPHome security node)
opts.d: Every intrusion device has its own cable to the SSC: Ethernet, battery, optional GSM; HA template alarm panel.
Shorter cables, no SSC; weaker against tampering.
Perimeter (contacts, sirens, keypad) to the SSC; interior motion to the RBX.

questions.q: 'Delete contents' on a LOCKED layer?

opts.d: Shows the lock message; unlock first.
One dialog does both.

questions.q: One-room RBX (one size smaller): set by hand or automatically?

opts.d: Right-click → Egyszobás kivitel; a check suggests it when an RBX serves exactly one room.
Ticked when the ghost serves one room; you can untick it.

questions.q: BASE with all three units in one column + an RBX on the same wall section — how strong is the warning?

opts.d: Allowed, shown as a warning (heat, service access).
A note, no warning badge.
Allowed to place, but the stage shows an error until moved.

questions.q: Which devices drag their linked route ends along when moved?

opts.d: RBX, BASE, Elosztó, SSC — golden and silver route ends follow.
Endpoints too: a socket moved along the wall pulls its ARM end.

questions.q: Security controller (SSC) default kind

opts.d: Our own; Ethernet + battery + optional GSM.
A certified panel; HA integrates it.

questions.q: Entry keypad: the Security KPD and the HMI panel's 'Belépési pont' variant overlap. Which wins?

opts.d: PAN keeps 'Érintőpanel'; its entry variant stays readable for old plans only.
You choose per project.

sections.title: Erősáram split and circuit presets (Wave M)
sections.note: The largest changes of the round. M1 migrates every existing stack.

questions.q: Split Erősáram how?
questions.why: Your text: three layers (dedikált / dugalj / világítás) with four colours. The cheap alternative colours the existing sub-layers.

opts.d: Dedikált körök · Dugaljak · Világítás (lamp + switch). Existing stacks are migrated on load.
No migration, ten times cheaper; not what the draft says.

questions.q: Migration: which new layer keeps the old Erősáram layer's id (and its visibility, lock, tint)?

opts.d: The two others are created next to it with the same settings.
Same, different keeper.
Three new layers; the old one is removed once empty.

questions.q: Shutter motors (SHU) go on which layer?

opts.d: A switched load with the same input logic as lamps.
A 230 V point on a room circuit.
Its own circuit.

questions.q: Colours
questions.why: Dedikált #6d4c41 (barna, darker than the B-bus #b07a2a) · Dugalj #c62828 (vörös) · Lámpa #ef7b72 (világospiros) · Kapcsoló #f08c2e (narancs).

opts.d: If #f08c2e looks too close to the A-bus amber #e6a800.

questions.q: Lamps and switches wired together first, an RBX later — build that wiring path now?
questions.why: Today the fill routes lamps and switches from the RBX (switch = RBX input, Q29).

opts.d: M1 only splits layers and colours; the fill still routes both from the RBX.
The fill routes switch → lamp directly in rooms with no RBX.

questions.q: Default MCB curve in the circuit list
questions.why: The cabinet calculation already uses C (ELO_RULES.mcb: '1C 10A', '1C 16A'). You mentioned B and C; every row can be toggled.

opts.d: Consistent with the existing cabinet numbers.

opts.t: B for lighting and sockets, C for motors and dedicated
opts.d: Common domestic practice.

questions.q: Right-click a szerelvénydoboz → pick a circuit type. Then?

opts.t: The box joins it, then pick mode
opts.d: The box becomes an endpoint; your next clicks add the circuit's other endpoints (K / Esc ends).
The circuit waits for endpoints; the box is not added.

questions.q: The preset catalogue (MATERIAL §5: 11 basic, 11 additional, 9 special)

opts.d: You edit it later in the app (it is editable and exportable).
Write the rows to add, remove or re-rate.
